domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: Role ambiguity and responsibility displacement
canonical_definition: Parties assume that governance, compliance or operational control belongs to someone else.

conditions: All AI systems involving internal teams, customers, providers, deployers, integrators or other third parties.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Does the case exhibit Role ambiguity and responsibility displacement: Parties assume that governance, compliance or operational control belongs to someone else.
Do implemented workflows, data paths or operations show vendor assurance treated as deployer assurance, overlapping ownership, or unowned integrated components?
Does current evidence test presence or scoped absence of Role ambiguity and responsibility displacement, or does it remain unknown?

antipattern_indicators: Vendor assurance is treated as deployer assurance

conditions: Refer verified role ambiguity and responsibility displacement to the accountable authority before progression where the condition materially affects the requested operating scope.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, GOVERN 2.1 (PDF p. 28), GOVERN 6.1 (PDF p. 29)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on role assignment, communication and governance of third-party dependencies. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

failure_mechanism: The declared or implemented control can be unreliable where different parties identify different owners for the same critical duty, or both omit an integrated component. The mechanism can have an operational effect where incident or approval records show an unowned handoff, or vendor assurance was substituted for the deployer's own control evidence.
potential_consequences: A critical governance or incident duty may remain unperformed across a handoff.

atomic_tests.test: Compare the effective governance and design records. Determine whether different parties identify different owners for the same critical duty, or both omit an integrated component. Identify the system scope and the record that supports each conclusion.

Trace actual configurations or activity for the assessed release. Determine whether incident or approval records show an unowned handoff, or vendor assurance was substituted for the deployer's own control evidence. Attribute each observation to the specific path, time and decision.

Independently review a chain-of-responsibility exercise covering internal teams, suppliers and subcontracted services from initiating event to closure. Record whether each material mechanism was tested, the observed result and the scope limitations.

required_evidence.title: Effective design and governance records
required_evidence.description: Review the versioned owner decision and relevant specifications for evidence of whether different parties identify different owners for the same critical duty, or both omit an integrated component. Preserve material conflict and applicability context.

required_evidence.title: Observed condition or enforcement trace
required_evidence.description: Use effective configuration or dated operational records to determine whether incident or approval records show an unowned handoff, or vendor assurance was substituted for the deployer's own control evidence. Identify the version, affected paths and period represented.

required_evidence.title: Executed scoped comparison
required_evidence.description: Provide a chain-of-responsibility exercise covering internal teams, suppliers and subcontracted services from initiating event to closure. Include current scope, expected results, observed results, retained evidence and unresolved cases.

required_evidence.title: Independent review and limitations
required_evidence.description: An independent reviewer confirms the assessed version, completeness of coverage, result, limitations and whether a material change requires a new test.

required_artifacts: A chain-of-responsibility exercise covering internal teams, suppliers and subcontracted services from initiating event to closure.
Current version and scope with all material failure paths and cases identified.
Expected and observed results, attributable records, and independent review of coverage and residual limitations.

sufficiency: Presence requires affirmative evidence for a material mechanism. Examine whether different parties identify different owners for the same critical duty, or both omit an integrated component, and separately check whether incident or approval records show an unowned handoff, or vendor assurance was substituted for the deployer's own control evidence. A supported mechanism may establish presence within its evidenced scope.
Keep unresolved or contradictory mechanisms UNKNOWN and preserve the competing records. Refer material interpretation conflicts to the accountable human authority.

Use TESTED_ABSENT only after a current, executed, successful and independently verified evaluation covers all material paths within scope. Use a chain-of-responsibility exercise covering internal teams, suppliers and subcontracted services from initiating event to closure. Reassess when material changes affect that scope.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A document can identify a declared gap. Effective configuration can demonstrate a reachable condition. Observed records support only their covered period and workflow. TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete scoped absence contract.
false_positive_guards: A shared duty can be valid when a named primary owner and escalation route are explicit and exercised.
Confirm that the observed or alleged condition applies to the current assessed release and a reachable path.
prohibited_inferences: A gap or UNKNOWN in A3 alone cannot establish AP-A3 presence.
Missing complaints, incident silence and unsuccessful collection cannot establish absence.
Model output and tactic selection grant no authority to approve, close a finding or accept risk.

finding_definitions.title: Design or intent shows role ambiguity and responsibility displacement
Implementation or operating evidence shows role ambiguity and responsibility displacement
Presence or tested absence of role ambiguity and responsibility displacement is unresolved within scope
